chunks: I wrote to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) asking him about something concerning Tawheed. So he wrote back to me in his own handwriting: 'Praise belongs to God, Who inspires His servants to praise Him.'

He mentioned similar to what Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated, up to his words: 'and His existence has suppressed the wanderings of imaginations.' Then he added: 'The first thing in religion regarding Him is recognising Him; and the perfection of recognising Him is affirming His Oneness; and the perfection of affirming His Oneness is the negation of attributes from Him — by the testimony of every attribute that it is other than the One described, and the testimony of the One described that He is other than the attribute, and their joint testimony together that duality is impossible for the Eternal.'

So whoever describes God has limited Him, and whoever limits Him has numbered Him, and whoever numbers Him has negated His eternality. And whoever says 'How?' has sought to describe Him; and whoever says 'In what?' has contained Him; and whoever says 'Upon what?' has been ignorant of Him; and whoever says 'Where?' has isolated from Him; and whoever says 'What is He?' has attributed a nature to Him; and whoever says 'To what end?' has given Him a limit.

He was a Knower when there was nothing to be known, a Creator when there was no creation, and a Lord when there was nothing being nourished. And thus our Lord is described, and He is beyond what the describers describe Him as.

key_terms.التثنية: Al-tathniya — duality, the forbidden implication of twoness that arises when an attribute is posited as distinct from God
key_terms.التوحيد: Tawheed — Divine Unity, the affirmation that God is One; here specifically the highest form: negation of attributes
key_terms.المعرفة: Al-ma'rifa — gnosis, recognition, the intimate knowledge of God that is the first duty of religion
key_terms.نَفْيُ الصِّفَاتِ: Nafi al-sifat — negation of attributes; the doctrine that God transcends all descriptive categories

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia Imam's teaching on the negation of divine attributes in Tawheed?
ai.summary: This hadith is a written response from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS), the seventh Imam, to a disciple who inquired about the nature of Divine Oneness (Tawheed). The Imam expounds the highest level of Tawheed: the negation of attributes (nafi al-sifat), arguing that any positive description of God — however reverent — introduces duality by separating 'God' from 'His attribute.' He then enumerates the errors implicit in every common theological question ('How?', 'Where?', 'What?'), showing that each question-word smuggles in a creaturely limitation. The hadith concludes with the supreme formulation: God was Knower, Creator, and Lord before any of these relational categories applied — affirming His absolute transcendence. This teaching reflects the Mu'tazilite-influenced but distinctively Imami doctrine that attributes, if not negated as separate from the Divine Essence, imply plurality in God.
word_analysis: sought to describe Him (asked for His description)
anything to be known (object of knowledge)

en.hubeali: And Muhammad Bin Al Husayn reported, from Salih Bin Hamza, from Fatah Bin Abdullah, a slave of the Clan of Hashim who said, ‘I wrote to Abu Ibrahimasws (7th Imamasws) asking himasws about something from the Tawheed (Oneness). So heasws wrote to me in hisasws own handwriting: ‘The Praise is for Allahazwj, the Inspirer of Hisazwj servants to praise Himazwj’.

He (the narrator) mentioned similar to what Sahl Bin Ziyad narrated (Previous Hadeeth), up to hisasws words: ‘and Hisazwj Existence has Suppressed the wanderings of the imaginations’. Then there is an increase in it: ‘The first (matter) to make a Religion with is to recognise Himazwj, and the perfection of Hisazwj recognition is Hisazwj Tawheed (Oneness), and the perfection of Hisazwj Tawheed (Oneness) is the negation of the descriptions from Himazwj by testifying that every description, it is other than the described, and the testimony of the describer that Heazwj is other than the description, and the two testimonies together with the impossibility of the second from Himazwj (existing) in the eternity.

So the one who describes Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so he has limited Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and the one who limits Him<sup>azwj</sup>, so he has numbered Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and the one who numbers Him<sup>azwj</sup> so he has negated His<sup>azwj</sup> eternality, and the one who says, ‘How’, so he has described Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and the one who says, ‘In what’, so he has contained Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and the one who says, ‘Upon what’, so he has been ignorant of Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and the one who says, ‘Where’, so he has isolated from Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and the one who says, ‘What is He<sup>azwj</sup>’, so he has attributed Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and the one who says, ‘To what’, so he has given Him<sup>azwj</sup> an end-point.

He<sup>azwj</sup> was a Knower when there was nothing to be known, and a Creator when there was no creation, and a Lord<sup>azwj</sup> where there was nothing being Nourished. And that is how our<sup>asws</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> is described, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is Above what the describers are describing Him<sup>azwj</sup> as’.
en.sarwar: 6. The above is narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Salih ibn Hamza from Fath ibn ‘Abdallah Mawla Banu Hashim who has said the following. “I wrote to abu Ibrahim (a.s.) asking him about the Oneness of Allah.” He wrote back to me in his own hand writing, “All praise is due to Allah, Who inspires His servants with His praise.”

He mentioned in it facts similar to those in the Hadith of Sahl ibn Ziyad (No. 5 above) to his words that read, ‘His essence has uprooted the (spreading) vines of imaginations’ with the following addition. “The first thing in His religion is to know Him. A perfect knowledge about Him is to know that He is One. A perfect belief in His Oneness is to negate all attributes from Him. Every attribute is evidence that it is different from what it is attributed to. That everything to which an attribute is ascribed is evidence that it is something other than the attribute. Both the attribute and to whatever it is attributed are evidence that there are two things which invalidate His being eternal.

Whoever attributes a quality to Allah he has considered Him limited. Whoever considers Him limited he has enumerated Him and whoever enumerates Him he has considered His eternity invalid. Whoever says how is He, he has he has considered Him describable. Whoever says in what is He, he has considered Him as contained. Whoever says on what is He, he has become ignorant of Him. Whoever says where is He, he has considered some place without Him. Whoever says what is He, he has attributed certain qualities to Him. Whoever says up to what limit is He, he has considered Him as having an end.

He had knowledge before there was anything to know. He was the Creator before there was any creatures. He was the Lord before there was a worshipper. Thus, is our Lord spoken of and it is above the way others speak of Him.”
